Diagnostic reconstruction of calculated Table III P-V-T outputs; it neither reproduces the published analytical model nor replaces the source pressure standard. Cold BM3 V0 is Vc at 0 K (ambient volume Vc/cold\_volume\_ratio); phonon and electronic pressures are absolute relative to 0 K. Electronic pressure is assumed volume independent and linearly interpolated, not extrapolated; no caloric potential is supplied.

Pt measurements bracketing each scan retain their source first/last sequence labels. Phase labels distinguish bcc-Fe from hcp-Fe and NaCl-B1 from NaCl-B2. The workbook defines the errors as standard errors combining peak-fitting standard deviations and dispersion among volumes from different (hkl) peaks. Cu reference volumes are included even though no separate Shen-Smith Cu EOS record is bundled. The complete workbook is retained rather than only the lower-scatter run subsets used for the preferred fits.

### gold\_anderson\_1989\_table1\_thermodynamic\_inputs

- **Description:** The 20 printed Table I rows of heat capacity, volume expansivity, and ultrasonic elastic modes assembled by Anderson et al. from seven earlier sources. These are property-level inputs to a staged thermodynamic construction, not P-V-T observations sharing a regression objective.
- **Kind:** heterogeneous\_thermodynamic\_compilation
- **Reference:**
    - **Authors:** Anderson; Isaak; Yamamoto
    - **Year:** 1989
    - **Title:** Anharmonicity and the equation of state for gold
    - **Source:** J. Appl. Phys.
    - **Volume:** 65
    - **Locator:** 1534-1543
    - **DOI:** 10.1063/1.342969
- **Source location:** Section II, Equations (4)-(5), and Table I, page 1535
- **Associated EOS records:** gold\_anderson\_1989\_bm3\_1
- **Uncertainty:**
    - **Elastic constants:** The paper states 0.5% accuracy for the measured elastic constants; the source studies report about 1% uncertainty for their temperature derivatives.
    - **Other properties:** No row-wise uncertainty or covariance is printed.
- **Notes:** The two 300 K elastic rows are retained separately. Table I visibly prints Cp=1.1288 at 300 K. That number breaks the smooth sequence and yields gamma=3.395 through Equation (12), whereas Table IV prints gamma=2.974. Equation (4) gives 1.28820 and inversion of Equation (12) with the printed Table III Ks and Table IV gamma gives 1.28843, so cp\_reconstructed\_0p1\_j\_g\_k records 1.2888 as the evident intended value while preserving the literal print in the adjacent column. Low-temperature expansivities were obtained by graphical smoothing and are not independently reproducible from the article alone.

[Observation resource](https://github.com/CPrescher/peritheos/blob/main/peritheos/data/datasets/gold-anderson-1989-table1-thermodynamic-inputs.csv)
